title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services

reading.body:
This incident is an impersonation fraud in which scammers used AI-generated video to create a false likeness of a real, named attorney and deployed it across multiple social media platforms to solicit payment for immigration services that were never delivered. The failure sits entirely outside any AI product the attorney or his office controls. The AI here was a tool in the hands of bad actors, used to fabricate convincing video content at scale, not a deployed system that malfunctioned in the conventional sense.

What made the scheme effective was the combination of synthetic media, volume, and platform reach. Nearly 6,500 fake profiles were created across TikTok, Facebook, and Instagram before an anti-piracy company helped remove them. The transaction pipeline moved victims off public platforms and into private messaging on WhatsApp, then collected payment through peer-to-peer apps that offer little recourse. No human check internal to the scam operation was available to victims, and the platforms did not catch the profiles before significant harm occurred.

What is not established is who is responsible for creating or running the operation, whether any law enforcement investigation has produced findings, or how many victims suffered financial loss beyond the cases reported.

reports.title: Scammers steal identity of renowned Miami attorney to target immigrants on social media
South Florida immigration attorney says AI scammers are using his identity to target immigrants
Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
Angel Leal, a South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience, has become the victim of an elaborate AI-powered scam targeting vulnerable immigrants. Criminals have created hundreds of fake social media profiles and AI-generated videos depicting Leal offering fraudulent immigration services, including promises of US residency for $2,200. The scams escalated dramatically in recent months after potential clients began calling his office about services he never provided. Leal discovered fake accounts on TikTok, Facebook, and Instagram, with an anti-piracy company helping remove nearly 6,500 profiles across these platforms.

The scammers typically use social media videos to direct victims to contact numbers via WhatsApp, where they exchange emails and phony contracts before requesting payment through apps like Venmo, Zelle, or Cash App. Fake testimonials feature supposed clients praising Leal for obtaining legal status or securing releases from immigration detention. Leal warns immigrants to verify the identity of legal service providers and avoid those requesting immediate payment through digital payment apps. He has changed his personal phone number and plans to contact local and federal authorities to investigate the fraud.
